title: Noon runtime quicklog — triage & micro-tasks
content:
Quick midday dump — small checkpoints, hypotheses, and next-day micro-tasks. Rough and unordered.

Context:
- Noticed a mild bump in P95 on the dedicated pools after the 03/09 rollout of default small-batch policy. Mostly in requests with long context (>=2048).
- Suspect combination of prefix cache misses + eviction thrash when multiple short/long sessions interleave.

What I observed (logs + quick grep):
- 2026-03-10 11:41:22: spike on pod gpu-rt-14 (zone us-west2). Token throughput drops ~18%.
- Kernel logs show repeated KV-store eviction logs: "evict candidate: 32MB" every ~300ms during spike window.
- Repro steps (fast): curl hosted-api/… with two sessions: one with prompt len 256 repeated, one with prompt len 4096 streamed.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Eviction policy too aggressive for mixed seq-len workloads -> frequent cache rebuilds cost. (most likely)
2) Small-batch autoscaler created slightly smaller workers, changing sequence-length distribution per-worker -> cache miss rate increases.
3) New kernel path for attention >4096 falls back to slower kernel causing burst latency.

Immediate triage checklist (what I did / to do):
- [x] Pull SLO traces for 03/09-03/11 and compare p50/p95/p99 by sequence bucket. (quick notebook saved to linked PR)
- [x] Add debug counter to KV manager to emit "cache-size-by-session" at 1s resolution (temp flag on rt).
- [ ] Re-run the two-session curl test with DEBUG=kv on gpu-rt-14 (need ~30 min window)
- [ ] Try reducing eviction aggression by +25% on canary (env KV_EVICT_HEADROOM=1.25) and smoke.
- [ ] Run micro-bench with curated workload (mix 70% short(<=512), 30% long(4096)) on local qemu gpu to see rebuild penalty.

Notes on potential quick fixes:
- Soft fix: increase per-session cache quota for workers tagged "high-mem" (cheap config flip). Risk: increased memory fragmentation.
- Mid fix: change eviction heuristic to prefer evicting oldest-completely-unused prefixes rather than newest-first. That requires adjusting eviction comparator (TODO: proto change).
- Longer: implement small sticky routing: route long seq sessions to nodes with "long-cache" profile. Needs routing + billing/placement check.

Commands & quick reproducer (save these):
- repro short+long: bash -c '\nfor i in 1 2; do \n  curl -s -X POST $HOST/generate -d @short.json & \n  curl -s -X POST $HOST/generate -d @long.json & \ndone'
- collect kernel logs: sudo journalctl -u runtime-kernel -o short-iso --since "2026-03-09" | grep -i evict > /tmp/evict.log

To communicate:
- Ping @ashap in #serving-runtime with quick summary + link to this note.
- Add one-liner to standup: "Investigating P95 bump tied to KV eviction thrash; trying config canary + repro."

Open questions / things to jot down:
- Are there any recent model onboardings that changed tokenization behavior? (search releases)
- Did Dedicated pool autoscaler change instance mix for us-west2 last week? (ask infra)
- Does canary with KV_EVICT_HEADROOM=1.25 keep memory safety tests green? Need SRE signoff.

Small TODOs for tomorrow (bite-sized):
- [ ] Reproduce locally and capture p95 numbers (target: before/after change)
- [ ] Draft short PR to emit per-session KV-hit-rate metric (name: runtime.kv.session_hit_rate)
- [ ] Add ticket to infra for sticky routing feasibility (include cost delta estimate)
- [ ] Quick runbook blurb for oncall: if P95 > 1500ms and eviction logs > 1000/hr, flip KV_EVICT_HEADROOM canary

Random scratch:
- Idea: keep a tiny LRU of the top-k most-recently-used prefixes across sessions to reduce rebuild cost for long/short mixes. Could be bounded by aggregate tokens rather than bytes.
- Note to self: write small microbenchmark harness that simulates 100 concurrent sessions with configurable seq-len distribution. Reuse bench/seqsim from tools/bench.

Endnotes:
- Save cleaned notes -> put in shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/investigations/ once validated.
- If I get stable repro and canary shows improvement, propose small rollout over next 48h.

— Harper
(quick: 35m)
